newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ZAMBIA SAYS SPEEDY PRIVATISATION PLAN ON TRACK.
newsitem.headline: ZAMBIA SAYS SPEEDY PRIVATISATION PLAN ON TRACK.

text.p: The Zambian government reiterated on Thursday its commitment to the speedy privatisation of state assets and said it hoped all sale agreements would be concluded by year end.

Addressing an African Mining conference Zambia's Minister of Mines and Mineral Development, Christon Tembo, said the deadline for bids for Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines Ltd (ZCCM), the jewel in the state's asset crown, was the end of February.
"We remain hopeful that during the course of 1997 all agreements within the whole process of privatisation will be concluded," Tembo said.

He said Zambia had, since the start of the privatisation programme four years ago, successfully concluded the sale of 165 parastatals. The programme is regarded by some economic analysts as Africa's most successful.

The privatisation of ZCCM, the biggest state-owned company, began last month with the sale of an 80 percent stake in Kansanshi copper mine to the U.S.-based Cyprus Amax Minerals Company for $28 million.
"This process is going on smoothly and it has reached an advanced stage," Tembo said.
The privatisation of ZCCM, which earns around 90 percent of the country's foreign exchange earnings, is seen as crucial to the survival of Zambia's mining industry.

Tembo said ZCCM, in which government holds a 60 percent stake, Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd a 27 percent holding and private investors the balance, saw production peak at 700,000 tonnes during the 1970s.
Production had since declined steadily reaching 310,000 tonnes in 1995/96.

"It was quite clear to government that once capital was injected production would improve," Tembo said, adding that the privatisation had drawn interest from companies in South Africa, North America, India, Japan, Europe and Canada.
Other state mining and gemstone operations would also be privatised, Tembo said.
Late in January, the Zambia Privatisation Agency said it had sold the Mindeco Small Mines Ltd as a going concern for 183 million kwacha ($140,000).
A deal on the development of another ZCCM mine, Konkola Deep, is expected this month when a final memorandum of understanding is signed between the government and a consortium led by Anglo.
The consortium is expected to invest about $600 million to develop the project.
Another ZCCM asset, Konkola North has been offered for development to South Africa's Anglovaal Ltd and an option agreement is to be signed soon.
